limits: Built by reading source text, not by running the app. A row marked Good means the screen exists and every endpoint it calls is registered; it does not mean a person has clicked through it with real data.
A screen is linked to endpoints by following its imports three levels deep. Calls made further away are not seen, so "API calls" can undercount; those rows are marked Check.
Tables are linked to a feature through the backend FILE that serves its endpoints, so a feature can list tables a neighbouring route in the same file uses.

"Called by the web app: No" covers device endpoints (SMS gateway, bus tracker), background jobs, public pages and routes whose path the web app builds from variables. It is a list to review, not a list of dead code.
The Go server (internal/) that production ran before the Workers move is not inventoried here; this is the Worker backend, the React web app and the D1 schema.
seller: Only a support account could be created from the console, and nobody could be suspended, re-roled or given a new password without SQL on the platform database.

Team screen now lists everyone and can add a seller administrator or support person, suspend with a reason (signs them out at once), reactivate, change role and reset a password. Guards: nobody changes their own access, a super admin is only changed by a super admin, the last active seller administrator cannot be suspended or demoted. Every change is written to platform_events.
A support account held no screen: it signed in to an empty console and could not open the ticket queue (the queue needed the right to edit tenants).
A support login now holds the Support queue screen and only that. Ticket routes are gated on the queue, not on tenant editing.
The queue screen draws hours open, hours promised for the plan and "past what we promised", but its route never sent those figures, so the SLA display never appeared.
The route now sends open_hours, promised_hours, breached and the plan for every ticket.
"Take" changed the status but could not record who took it: assigned_to points at the school's own users.
Tenant migration 0024 adds the vendor agent (id and name). Whoever on the desk first acts on a ticket holds it, and both the vendor queue and the school see the name.

A support session ("enter this school, say why, for how long") could never be saved: the table referenced a school user and the operator is a platform account. And nothing checked for a session, so any support login could name any school and read its shape, jobs and audit trail.

Tenant migration 0025 rebuilds the table without that reference. A support login is now outside every school unless it has a live, unexpired session recorded in that school; the school's administrator can see it and end it. Any platform account can open a session for itself with a reason of at least 8 characters, for at most 4 hours.

Seller administrators and super admins still enter any school without recording a session. That is deliberate for now (running the console means entering schools all day), but their changes inside a school are not attributed in the school's audit log.
Decide whether operators must also record a reason, and write operator actions into the school's audit trail.
Platform accounts have no MFA; the table has no column for it.
Add MFA for platform users (control migration, mfa.ts, login).
A new account gets a one-time password shown on screen to hand over; there is no emailed invite link, and a platform account is not forced to change the password at first sign-in.
Add an invite/first-sign-in flow once outgoing email for the platform is settled.

A ticket has a subject, a body and a status. There is no reply thread, no history and no notification to the school when the vendor acts. No screen in a school's console raises a vendor ticket (the endpoint exists).
Add a thread table, a school-side "Contact support" screen and notifications.
What was promised is a fixed table in code keyed on plan codes (enterprise, pro, basic…); a plan with another code gets the slowest tier.
Store the promise on the plan.
Invoices, payments, dunning and auto-suspend are real. Checkout creates an order but calls no payment provider; outside production it simulates success.
Needs a provider decision (e.g. Razorpay) and its keys: create the order with the provider and verify its webhook.
Run as dry runs unless CF_API_TOKEN, CF_ACCOUNT_ID and D1_ADMIN_LIVE=true are set on the Worker.
Set the secrets when ready; document them.
Tenants, plans, limits, provisioning, lifecycle, export, billing ledger, audit, board members
